examples: The board decided to appoint her as the new chief executive.
هیئت‌مدیره تصمیم گرفت او را به عنوان مدیرعامل جدید منصوب کند.
The judge will appoint a lawyer for anyone who cannot afford one.
قاضی برای هر کسی که نتواند وکیل استخدام کند، یک وکیل منصوب خواهد کرد.
The committee appointed three new members to oversee the budget.
آن کمیته سه عضو جدید را برای نظارت بر بودجه منصوب کرد.
miniContext: To appoint someone means to formally choose or assign them to a position, role, or duty, usually without an election. A company's board can appoint a new executive, just as a court can appoint a lawyer to represent someone in need. The word always implies an official decision made by a person or group with the authority to decide. Once appointed, a person typically holds the position until they resign, are replaced, or their term ends.

examples: Even kings and queens are mortal, no matter how much power they hold.
حتی پادشاهان و ملکه‌ها هم فانی هستند، هر چقدر هم که قدرت داشته باشند.
The soldier suffered a mortal wound and died before help could arrive.
آن سرباز زخمی مهلک برداشت و قبل از اینکه کمک برسد، جان داد.
Facing a mortal illness forced him to think seriously about what truly mattered.
روبه‌رو شدن با یک بیماری مهلک او را وادار کرد جدی به آنچه واقعاً اهمیت داشت فکر کند.
miniContext: Mortal describes anything subject to death, reminding us that every living being eventually dies, no matter their power or status. A mortal wound or mortal illness is one serious enough to cause death, often used in dramatic or literary contexts. The word also appears in phrases like "mortal enemy," referring to an opponent considered dangerous enough to cause death. Thinking about being mortal often leads people to reflect more deeply on the meaning of their lives.

examples: The previous occupant of the apartment left behind several boxes of old books.
ساکن قبلی آن آپارتمان چند جعبه کتاب قدیمی از خودش به جا گذاشته بود.
Firefighters safely evacuated every occupant from the burning building.
آتش‌نشانان هر ساکن آن ساختمان در حال سوختن را با امنیت تخلیه کردند.
Only one occupant was in the car when it was pulled over by police.
فقط یک سرنشین در آن ماشین بود وقتی پلیس آن را متوقف کرد.
miniContext: An occupant is a person who lives in, uses, or is present inside a particular space, such as a house, vehicle, or building. Landlords often need to know who the current occupant of a property is for legal and safety reasons. In emergencies, rescue workers focus first on getting every occupant safely out of a dangerous building. The word can also describe a passenger in a vehicle, referring to anyone inside it at a given moment.

examples: Artists often depict quiet village scenes in paintings like this one.
هنرمندان اغلب صحنه‌های آرام روستایی را در نقاشی‌هایی مثل این به تصویر می‌کشند.
The documentary aims to depict the daily struggles of refugees honestly.
آن فیلم مستند سعی دارد مبارزات روزانه پناهجویان را به‌طور صادقانه به تصویر بکشد.
Historians argue that the film fails to depict the war accurately.
تاریخ‌نگاران استدلال می‌کنند که آن فیلم موفق نمی‌شود آن جنگ را به‌درستی به تصویر بکشد.
miniContext: To depict something means to represent or show it, usually through art, writing, or film, rather than describing it directly in words. A painting can depict a peaceful landscape, while a documentary might depict the harsh realities of life in a war zone. Critics and historians often debate whether a particular depiction is accurate or fair to the people and events involved. The word applies broadly across visual and narrative art forms, wherever something is being represented rather than simply stated.

examples: Archaeologists discovered an ancient burial site beneath the old farmland.
باستان‌شناسان یک محل باستانی دفن را زیر آن زمین کشاورزی قدیمی کشف کردند.
Construction on the new hospital site is expected to begin next spring.
ساخت‌وساز در محل بیمارستان جدید انتظار می‌رود بهار آینده آغاز شود.
The company chose a site near the river for its new factory.
آن شرکت یک محل نزدیک به رودخانه را برای کارخانه جدیدش انتخاب کرد.
miniContext: A site is a specific location, especially one chosen or used for a particular purpose, such as construction, archaeology, or history. Archaeologists spend years carefully excavating a single site, uncovering clues about how people lived long ago. Developers must evaluate a potential site carefully before building anything, considering factors like access, cost, and environmental impact. The word applies to almost any place being studied, built on, or set aside for a specific activity.

examples: She memorized the first verse of the poem for her literature class.
او بیت اول آن شعر را برای کلاس ادبیاتش از حفظ کرد.
The song's second verse tells a much sadder story than the chorus suggests.
بیت دوم آن آهنگ داستانی بسیار غم‌انگیزتر از آنچه ترانه تکرار می‌گوید، روایت می‌کند.
He prefers reading verse to prose because of its rhythm and sound.
او به دلیل ریتم و آهنگش، خواندن شعر را به نثر ترجیح می‌دهد.
miniContext: Verse refers to writing arranged with rhythm and often rhyme, typically in the form of poetry or song lyrics. A poem or song is usually divided into sections called verses, each one developing the story or feeling a little further. Students studying literature often memorize a particular verse to analyze its structure, rhythm, and meaning closely. More broadly, the word verse can also describe poetic writing in general, as distinct from ordinary prose.

examples: He ate a quarter of the pizza and saved the rest for later.
او یک‌چهارم آن پیتزا را خورد و بقیه را برای بعد نگه داشت.
The company's profits increased significantly during the final quarter of the year.
سود آن شرکت در سه‌ماهه پایانی سال به طور قابل‌توجهی افزایش یافت.
Soldiers were given quarters near the base for the duration of the training.
به سربازان در نزدیکی پایگاه برای مدت آن دوره آموزشی محل اسکان داده شد.
miniContext: Quarter has several related meanings: one-fourth of something, a three-month period of the business year, or temporary living space, usually for soldiers or workers. A company reports its earnings every quarter, giving investors a regular update on financial performance. Soldiers and workers stationed away from home are often provided with quarters, basic housing close to where they work. Despite the different contexts, each meaning of quarter relates to a defined portion, whether of time, space, or a whole object.

examples: The journalist asked permission to quote the senator directly in her article.
آن خبرنگار اجازه خواست تا مستقیماً از آن سناتور در مقاله‌اش نقل قول کند.
Students must quote their sources properly to avoid being accused of plagiarism.
دانش‌آموزان باید منابع خود را به‌درستی نقل قول کنند تا متهم به سرقت ادبی نشوند.
He loves to quote famous philosophers whenever he gives a speech.
او عاشق این است که هر وقت سخنرانی می‌کند، از فیلسوفان مشهور نقل قول کند.
miniContext: To quote someone means to repeat their exact words, either in speech or in writing, giving credit to the original speaker or author. Journalists must be careful to quote their sources accurately, since misquoting someone can damage trust and credibility. Academic writing requires students to quote properly, using citations to show exactly where an idea or sentence came from. The word can also apply to repeating memorable lines from books, speeches, or films in everyday conversation.

examples: The scientist proposed a novel solution that no one had considered before.
آن دانشمند راه‌حلی نو و بدیع پیشنهاد داد که هیچ‌کس قبلاً به آن فکر نکرده بود.
Her novel approach to teaching math made the subject far less intimidating.
رویکرد نو او در تدریس ریاضی، آن موضوع را بسیار کمتر ترسناک کرد.
The technology seemed novel at the time, though it is common today.
آن فناوری در آن زمان نو و بدیع به نظر می‌رسید، هرچند امروز رایج است.
miniContext: Novel, as an adjective, describes something new, original, or unlike anything tried before. Scientists and inventors are praised for a novel approach that solves an old problem in an unexpected way. Teachers who find a novel method of explaining a difficult subject often make learning feel easier and more engaging. Something that feels novel today may eventually become ordinary once it is widely adopted and no longer surprises anyone.

examples: Bright flowers attract bees and other pollinating insects.
گل‌های رنگارنگ زنبورها و دیگر حشرات گرده‌افشان را جذب می‌کنند.
The museum's new exhibit is expected to attract thousands of visitors.
انتظار می‌رود نمایشگاه جدید آن موزه هزاران بازدیدکننده را جذب کند.
Her confident personality naturally attracts people wherever she goes.
شخصیت باعتمادبه‌نفس او به طور طبیعی هر جا که می‌رود افراد را جذب می‌کند.
miniContext: To attract means to draw something or someone closer through appeal, interest, or natural pull. Bright colors and sweet scents attract insects to flowers, helping plants reproduce through pollination. Businesses design advertisements specifically to attract new customers, hoping to stand out among many competitors. The word also applies to personal qualities, as when someone's charm or confidence naturally attracts friends and admirers.

examples: The novel raises difficult questions about morality and personal responsibility.
آن رمان سؤالات دشواری درباره اخلاق و مسئولیت شخصی مطرح می‌کند.
Different cultures sometimes disagree sharply on matters of morality.
فرهنگ‌های مختلف گاهی در مسائل مربوط به اخلاق به‌شدت اختلاف نظر دارند.
He questioned the morality of profiting from other people's suffering.
او اخلاقی بودن سودجویی از رنج دیگران را زیر سؤال برد.
miniContext: Morality concerns the principles that distinguish right from wrong, shaping how people judge their own and others' behavior. Philosophers have debated questions of morality for centuries, trying to define what makes an action genuinely good or bad. Works of literature often explore morality through difficult choices faced by their characters, forcing readers to consider their own values. Because morality can vary across cultures and time periods, people frequently disagree about where exactly its boundaries lie.

examples: Wild horses still roam freely across parts of the western plains.
اسب‌های وحشی هنوز به‌طور آزاد در بخش‌هایی از دشت‌های غربی پرسه می‌زنند.
As a child, she loved to roam the woods behind her grandmother's house.
او در کودکی عاشق پرسه زدن در جنگل‌های پشت خانه مادربزرگش بود.
Tourists are free to roam the old city streets without a guide.
گردشگران آزادند بدون راهنما در خیابان‌های شهر قدیمی پرسه بزنند.
miniContext: To roam means to wander around an area freely, without a fixed destination or purpose. Wild animals roam across large territories in search of food, while curious children often roam nearby fields and forests just to explore. Travelers sometimes prefer to roam unfamiliar cities on foot, discovering unexpected sights rather than following a strict itinerary. The word suggests a relaxed, open-ended kind of movement, driven more by curiosity than by any particular goal.
